    - text: PHASE 1 · STATISTICAL INFERENCE
    - heading "Type I and Type II Error" [level=1]
    - paragraph: See the decision trade-off. At fixed n and true effect, lowering α reduces false positives but raises false negatives.
    - text: "#2015 · 17 min · Advanced · Statistical Inference"
    - heading "Decision Trade-off Lab" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Compare Type I error, Type II error and power for independent normal observations with known σ = 6.
    - button "How to read this"
    - img "Null and alternative sample-mean distributions with computed error and power areas": "Null: μ₀ = 50 Comparison mean: μ₁ = 56.00 Sample-mean SD = 1.000 Sample-mean SD = 1.000 44.0 46.0 48.0 50.0 52.0 54.0 56.0 58.0 60.0 62.0 0.00 0.10 0.20 0.30 0.40 51.645 Sample mean x̄ · dashed lines: critical cutoff(s)"
    - text: "H₀: μ = 50 True μ = 56.00 Critical cutoff"
    - article:
      - heading "Type I Error (α)" [level=3]
      - strong: "0.050"
      - paragraph: P(reject H₀ | H₀ true)
    - article:
      - heading "Type II Error (β)" [level=3]
      - strong: < 0.001
      - paragraph: P(fail to reject H₀ | specified H₁)
    - article:
      - heading "Power (1 − β)" [level=3]
      - strong: "> 0.999"
      - paragraph: P(reject H₀ | specified H₁)
    - article:
      - heading "Standardized separation" [level=3]
      - strong: "6.000"
      - paragraph: (μ₁ − μ₀) / SE
    - complementary:
      - heading "Controls" [level=3]
      - text: Significance level α
      - slider "Drag Significance level α": "0.05"
      - spinbutton "Significance level α": "0.05"
      - text: 0.001 to 0.2 True mean μ₁
      - slider "Drag True mean μ₁": "56"
      - spinbutton "True mean μ₁": "56"
      - text: 50 to 60 Sample size n
      - slider "Drag Sample size n": "36"
      - spinbutton "Sample size n": "36"
      - text: 10 to 200
      - heading "Test" [level=3]
      - group "Test sidedness":
        - button "One-sided (>)" [pressed]
        - button "Two-sided (≠)"
      - heading "Current Settings" [level=3]
      - math: "H 0 : μ = 50"
      - math: "H 1 : μ > 50"
      - paragraph: σ = 6 (known); n = 36
      - paragraph: SE = 6 / √36 = 1.000
      - paragraph: d = (56.00 − 50) / 1.000 = 6.000
      - paragraph: z critical = 1.645
      - paragraph: "x̄ cutoff(s): 51.645"
    - article:
      - heading "Decision Framework" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Reject H₀ when x̄ > 51.645.
      - text: H₀ true (μ = 50) H₁ true (μ = 56.00) Reject H₀
      - button "Type I Error (α) False positive 0.050" [pressed]:
        - strong: Type I Error (α)
        - text: False positive 0.050
      - button "Correct Decision (Power) True positive when an effect exists > 0.999":
        - strong: Correct Decision (Power)
        - text: True positive when an effect exists > 0.999
      - text: Fail to reject H₀
      - button "Correct Decision True negative 0.950":
        - strong: Correct Decision
        - text: True negative 0.950
      - button "Type II Error (β) False negative when an effect exists < 0.001":
        - strong: Type II Error (β)
        - text: False negative when an effect exists < 0.001
      - paragraph: Rejecting a true null hypothesis creates a false alarm.
    - article:
      - 'heading "Scenario: Medical Screening" [level=2]':
        - img
        - text: "Scenario: Medical Screening"
      - paragraph: A screening test flags a possible disease. This illustrates decision errors, not a diagnostic model or clinical recommendation.
      - paragraph: "H₀: disease absent. H₁: disease present."
      - img
      - text: Type I Error (False Positive)
      - paragraph: A healthy person is flagged as potentially having disease.
      - img
      - text: Type II Error (False Negative)
      - paragraph: A person with disease is missed by the screen.
      - paragraph: Choosing α balances the consequences of errors. Predictive values also depend on prevalence; α and β alone do not give them.
